title: Canary Scheduler: Cost-Aware Deployment & Rollback Design Spec
author: Aisha Kapoor
summary: Design for a Canary Scheduler that balances deployment safety with runtime economics by dynamically adjusting canary traffic, model variants, and rollback thresholds based on real-time cost and SLO signals.
body:
Overview

This design spec defines the Canary Scheduler: a control-plane component of Redwood that manages staged rollouts of model variants and runtime configuration with explicit cost-awareness. The scheduler’s goal is to maximize safe throughput delivered to customers while minimizing per-token runtime cost and reducing unnecessary full-rollbacks. It tightly integrates with observability, Optimize recommendations, and the routing layer.

Key objectives

- Make canary rollouts safer by incorporating cost signals alongside latency/error SLOs.
- Reduce unnecessary escalation to full rollback by enabling traffic diversion to cheaper compatible variants when quality is acceptable.
- Provide transparent, auditable decision logs and guardrails for commercial and compliance review.
- Enable rapid automated rollback or safe ramp-up when signals meet defined policies.

Scope and non-goals

- In scope: hosted and dedicated deployments; model variants and quantization profiles; per-route canary policies; cost-influenced ramp strategies; observability hooks and audit records.
- Out of scope: on-prem air-gapped Private installations for initial rollout (will be supported in a follow-up), per-token billing changes, and UI surface (API-only in v1).

High-level flow

1. User creates a CanaryPlan via API referencing: source model variant(s), target routes, canary duration window, traffic steps, cost budget, SLO targets, and a rollback-policy.
2. Scheduler validates plan, queries Optimize for suggested batching/quantization profile, and evaluates compatibility with runtime kernels.
3. Scheduler initiates the canary by registering routing rules for the first traffic step and starts telemetry collection.
4. During the canary window, Scheduler computes a rolling evaluation every 1 minute combining: error rate, p95 latency, cost-per-1k-tokens (runtime metric), and quality delta from baseline (optional EVAL suite).
5. Based on the evaluation and the configured policy, Scheduler either: advance traffic, pause and hold, divert traffic to alternate compatible variant, or trigger rollback.

Decision inputs and signals

- SLO signals (primary safety signals):
  - error_rate (5xx and model-failure-rate)
  - latency_p95_ms
  - response-consistency/regression score (from lightweight eval capture)
- Cost signals (economic signals):
  - runtime_cost_per_1k_tokens (from runtime billing bridge)
  - GPU_utilization_efficiency and batching factor
  - projected monthly cost delta if canary ramps to 100%
- Observability signals:
  - trace error types, request trace samples, and KV-cache hit rates
  - token-level breakdowns (prompt vs generated)

Policy model (priority order)

1. If any SLO signal breaches hard threshold for >2 consecutive evaluation windows => immediate rollback to previous variant and create incident (severity S2).
2. If soft SLO degradation (marginal increase in latency_p95 or small regression) but cost savings > configured budget_delta and quality delta within tolerance => consider diversion to cheaper compatible variant and continue canary in reduced form.
3. If no SLO breaches and cost delta within acceptable range => advance according to traffic schedule.
4. If conflicting signals (cost improves but quality drops beyond tolerance) => pause and run gated evals (see gated-eval section).

Config schema (API request example)

POST /v1/canary-plans

Request body (YAML/JSON tolerated):

canary_plan:
  name: "conversational-v2-canary-2026-10-09"
  owner: "platform-chat-service"
  routes: ["/v1/chat/conversation", "/v1/chat/embeds"]
  baseline_variant: "gptx-13b-quant-16"
  canary_variants: ["gptx-13b-quant-8", "gptx-13b-quant-4-fp16"]
  traffic_schedule: [10, 30, 60, 100]  # percentages
  step_duration_minutes: 15
  total_window_minutes: 90
  cost_budget_percent_delta: -25  # expect cost decrease target
  slo_targets:
    latency_p95_ms: 220
    error_rate_pct: 0.5
  rollback_policy: "hard-on-slo-breach"
  alternate_variant_diversion: true
  gated_eval_suite_id: "conv-regression-30-prompts"

Operational parameters and thresholds

| Parameter | Default | Notes |
|-----------|---------|-------|
| evaluation_interval_minutes | 1 | Rolling window for decisioning |
| hard_slo_breach_window | 2 | Consecutive eval windows to trigger immediate rollback |
| soft_regression_tolerance_pct | 2.0 | Percent drop in regression score acceptable if cost gains exist |
| cost_savings_threshold_pct | 10 | Minimum runtime cost reduction to enable diversion |
| max_diversion_attempts | 2 | Number of times to try alternate variants before aborting |

Gated evaluation and human-in-the-loop

- When the policy reaches a pause state due to conflicting signals, the Scheduler will:
  1. Freeze traffic at current step.
  2. Run gated eval suite (if provided) capturing token-level diffs and sample outputs.
  3. Create a summary report and notify the owners via configured webhook and Slack channel.
  4. If the owner approves via API or UI (future), advance or divert; else rollback after configured grace period (default 30 minutes).

Alternative variant diversion logic

- Purpose: avoid full rollback when a cheaper compatible variant provides acceptable quality.
- Compatibility checks: model architecture match, tokenizer match, output schema compatibility, and runtime kernel compatibility.
- Diversion flow: choose highest-ranked alternative by Optimize score where quality_delta <= soft_regression_tolerance_pct and cost_savings >= cost_savings_threshold_pct.

Telemetry, audit and observability

- All decisions are written to the Canary Audit Log (immutable): plan_id, timestamp, evaluation_snapshot (SLOs, cost, variant metrics), and decision reason.
- Telemetry exports: per-minute canary metrics to long-term Observability (for correlation with billing).
- Alerting: immediate PagerDuty trigger on hard rollback incidents; low-priority tickets for soft pauses.

Crash and rollback runbooks (operations)

1. Automatic hard rollback executed by Scheduler: verify rollback success, validate baseline health (5 min), and escalate to oncall if post-rollback errors persist.
2. If alternate variant diversion was used and problems persist, escalate to model-owner and SRE to examine kernel/quantization mismatch.
3. For repeated canary instability (>3 failed rollouts in 30 days) the Scheduler will require manual approval for future automated rollouts for that model family.

Metrics and success criteria

- Safety: <1% of rollouts cause customer-visible degradation (post-rollback retention metric).
- Economics: average canary-led cost reduction when deployed to 100% >= 8% for quantization-driven rollouts.
- Speed: median time-to-rollback on hard SLO breach < 90s.

Compatibility matrix (extract)

| Runtime Kernel | Supported Variant Types | Notes |
|----------------|-------------------------|-------|
| kernel-v1      | fp32, fp16             | no quantized int support |
| kernel-v2      | int8, int4, fp16       | recommended for quant profiles |

Implementation plan and milestones

- Phase 0 (weeks 0-4): API schema and small prototype that can flip traffic in staging; basic telemetry hooks.
- Phase 1 (weeks 5-10): Integrate Optimize cost recommendations, implement decision engine, add audit log and webhooks.
- Phase 2 (weeks 11-16): Alternate variant diversion, gated eval integration, PagerDuty and incident automation.
- Phase 3 (weeks 17-22): Hardening, expanded runtime compatibility checks, limited enterprise beta with Dedicated customers.
